source_span.raw_source_excerpt: # Pronom personnel sujet de la [[deuxième personne du singulier]]. {{note}} Il désigne la personne à qui l’on parle, et peut être aussi bien masculin que féminin. C’est un pronom [[clitique]] ; cela signifie qu’il se trouve toujours à proximité du verbe dont il ne peut être séparé que par un autre pronom clitique ou par la particule négative ''[[ne]]'', soit immédiatement après le verbe dans l’[[inversion clitique]]. Dans tous les autres cas, on emploie ''{{lien|te|fr}}'' ou ''{{lien|toi|fr}}'' comme pronom personnel de la seconde personne du singulier.

* "Tu" is used to address one person in an informal situation. Older people tend to exclusively use it with familiar people, and do not use it with unfamiliar adults unless invited to; but younger people use this pronoun much more, using it together in any informal situation, even if they don't know each other. Using "vous" in this context will be seen as old-fashioned and distant.

usage.accepted_usage: Adverb expressing excess, including modification of an adjective or verb.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: Too/too much and 太/过量 express excess rather than the informal very intensifier. The adverb can modify an adjective or an action; the distinct trop de determiner construction is excluded.

usage.proposed_usage: Adjective describing something that corresponds to truth.
usage.scope_restrictions: Authenticity, hyperbole, Boolean values and noun or adverb uses are excluded.
usage.accepted_usage: Adjective describing something that corresponds to truth.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: True/conforme à la vérité/与事实相符 agree. The Chinese 正确的 is restricted by the following factual-truth explanation, rather than suggesting general suitability. Authenticity and Boolean values are excluded.

usage.proposed_usage: Masculine singular abstract noun for truth or what is true.
usage.scope_restrictions: The adjective, adverb and specialist Boolean value are excluded.
usage.accepted_usage: Masculine singular abstract noun for truth or what is true.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: The masculine singular abstract noun le vrai is truth/what is true, not the adjective or a Boolean constant. EN and ZH retain the abstract nominal reading and the source's truth scope.

usage.proposed_usage: Preposition introducing a person's home or place of activity.
usage.scope_restrictions: Figurative works, personal characteristics and among senses are excluded.
usage.accepted_usage: Preposition introducing a person's home or place of activity.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: The home/place-of-activity use agrees across languages. EN and ZH identify the person or stressed-pronoun complement. Narrowing to at someone's residence/workplace is legitimate; the country, author's works and among readings are excluded.

usage.proposed_usage: Feminine noun for a female child.
usage.scope_restrictions: Daughter as a family relationship, adult women and the obsolete or derogatory senses are excluded.
usage.accepted_usage: Feminine noun for a female child.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: A female child/girl/女童 agrees with the selected child definition. The separate daughter relationship and adult-woman readings are expressly excluded. The source's nonbinary form table supplies no extra selected sense here.

usage.proposed_usage: Plural definite article contracted with the preposition à, for both genders.
usage.scope_restrictions: This is not the possessive their or a general translation of à; uncontracted les remains distinct.
usage.accepted_usage: Plural definite article contracted with the preposition à, for both genders.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: The mandatory contraction is à + definite les, of either gender and plural. It is not possessive aux/their. EN and ZH properly explain that the rendering of à depends on construction, rather than promising one universal equivalent.

usage.proposed_usage: Masculine noun for the world as the Earth.
usage.scope_restrictions: People, social circles, the universe, imaginary worlds and religious senses are excluded.
usage.accepted_usage: Masculine noun for the world as the Earth.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: World means the Earth we live on. The source labels this an especially selected terrestrial sense. EN/ZH do not turn it into inhabitants, social circles, the universe or imaginary worlds.

usage.proposed_usage: Adjective describing a friendly or benevolent attitude.
usage.scope_restrictions: The noun friend, poetic favourable sense and colour terminology are excluded.
usage.accepted_usage: Adjective describing a friendly or benevolent attitude.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: Friendly/benevolent is adjectival, not the friend noun. Obligeant is retained as 乐于助人的. The adjective examples visage ami/langage ami support this use. The 1878 AMI adjective already supplies bienveillant/obligeant; amical is the current contributor synonym.

usage.proposed_usage: Masculine noun for a friend; the feminine counterpart is amie.
usage.scope_restrictions: Romantic partners, enthusiasts, allies and the language-name noun are excluded.
usage.accepted_usage: Masculine noun for a friend; the feminine counterpart is amie.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: Friend means a person linked by friendship. The masculine frozen form ami is preserved, with amie as the feminine counterpart only in usage. Romantic-partner and enthusiast senses remain excluded. The 1878 AMI entry corroborates the friendship relation.

usage.proposed_usage: Adjective retained in the fixed expression bon gré mal gré.
usage.scope_restrictions: No productive adjective meaning bad is implied; illness uses and the adverb or noun are excluded.
usage.accepted_usage: Adjective retained in the fixed expression bon gré mal gré.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: The adjective is deliberately limited to mal gré within bon gré mal gré. Current adjective L26-L27 expressly list the expression. EN and ZH distinguish the bad adjective component from the meaning of the whole expression: willingly or unwillingly/不管愿不愿意. The archaic productive adjective and illness predicate are excluded.

usage.proposed_usage: Adverb describing how an action is performed badly.
usage.scope_restrictions: Appearance, adjective uses and the noun pain are excluded.
usage.accepted_usage: Adverb describing how an action is performed badly.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: Badly and 不好地/错误地 describe an action's manner. The selected French incorrect/unsuitable-manner restriction is preserved. The longer source wording is independently found in DAF7 (1878), MAL, adverb paragraph; it is not dependent on a new 1935 formulation.

usage.proposed_usage: Masculine noun for physical pain, including avoir mal à.
usage.scope_restrictions: Illness as a diagnosis, moral evil, difficulty and harm are excluded.
usage.accepted_usage: Masculine noun for physical pain, including avoir mal à.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: Physical pain only is an accurate narrowing of source douleur physique, maladie. The disease diagnosis is excluded. Avoir mal à + body part is supported by the article and DAF7's physical-pain examples; the moral-evil noun is separate.

usage.proposed_usage: Adverb for a later time, with the reference time understood.
usage.scope_restrictions: The preposition with a complement, discourse contrast and the noun are excluded.
usage.accepted_usage: Adverb for a later time, with the reference time understood.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: Afterwards/later means an adverb with the reference time understood. Source L248 actually has Nous en parlerons après and L249 longtemps après. The conversational and then?/what follows? uses lower in the article are excluded. The author-composed example in the fields matches the contributor example.

usage.proposed_usage: Preposition marking temporal succession, as in après le repas.
usage.scope_restrictions: Spatial positions, ranks, regional progressive constructions and the adverb are excluded.
usage.accepted_usage: Preposition marking temporal succession, as in après le repas.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: Temporal after indicates posteriority relative to its complement. EN/ZH retain the preposition and do not include the regional progressive construction, spatial position or ranking senses.

usage.proposed_usage: Temporal adverb without an expressed complement, meaning beforehand or earlier.
usage.scope_restrictions: The preposition with an expressed complement, spatial progression and the adjective are excluded.
usage.accepted_usage: Temporal adverb without an expressed complement, meaning beforehand or earlier.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: All meaning fields follow the English Wiktionary French-section adverb beforehand/earlier at revision 92304586 L100, not the French spatial-depth adverb L159. The separate French adverb IPA at L158 applies to the same written headword. The reference time is implicit and the expressed-complement preposition is separate.

usage.proposed_usage: Preposition of temporal anteriority, as in avant le repas.
usage.scope_restrictions: Spatial order, priority in importance, avant de with an infinitive and the adverb are excluded.
usage.accepted_usage: Preposition of temporal anteriority, as in avant le repas.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: Temporal before marks anteriority. The explanation that the complement is later than the described action is directionally correct. Infinitival avant de, spatial ordering and importance are excluded.

usage.proposed_usage: Masculine noun for a need or necessity, including avoir besoin de.
usage.scope_restrictions: Poverty, bodily functions, financial terminology and the rare adjective are excluded.
usage.accepted_usage: Masculine noun for a need or necessity, including avoir besoin de.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: Need/necessity/需要 agrees with source nécessité. Avoir besoin de is supported at L58-L59, including both a thing and an infinitive. Poverty and bodily-function senses are excluded.

usage.proposed_usage: Masculine noun for consent or approval of a request.
usage.scope_restrictions: Musical chords, grammatical agreement, treaties and technical tuning are excluded.
usage.accepted_usage: Masculine noun for consent or approval of a request.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: Consent/approval of a request matches the selected approbation d'une demande, consentement. It does not silently generalize to a treaty, musical chord, tuning or grammatical agreement.

usage.proposed_usage: Plural possessive determiner; frozen Lexique subclass ADJ:pos is retained.
usage.scope_restrictions: Multiple possessors and singular possessed nouns are excluded; /se/ is the selected recorded IPA variant.
usage.accepted_usage: Plural possessive determiner; frozen Lexique subclass ADJ:pos is retained.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: Ses is a plural possessive determiner for one possessor, with nouns of either gender. EN/ZH distinguish the possessor's gender from the noun's gender; ses does not encode the possessor's sex. Current L17 expressly states one possessor and multiple objects. Frozen ADJ:pos is retained as the historical classification of the determiner, not a new lexical adjective claim.

usage.proposed_usage: Adjective describing beauty perceived by sight or hearing.
usage.scope_restrictions: Weather, size, in-law relationships and adverb or noun uses are excluded.
usage.accepted_usage: Adjective describing beauty perceived by sight or hearing.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: Beauty pleasant to sight or hearing is retained in beautiful/美的、漂亮的、动听的. The hearing component is not lost. Weather, quantity, in-law and adverb uses are excluded. The visible modern contributor definition differs from the DAF-era excellence noun.

usage.proposed_usage: Adverb restricted to avoir beau followed by an infinitive, expressing vain effort.
usage.scope_restrictions: The adjective beautiful, noun uses and the Quebec expression c'est beau are excluded.
usage.accepted_usage: Adverb restricted to avoir beau followed by an infinitive, expressing vain effort.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: The vain-effort avoir beau + infinitive use is explicit, distinct from beautiful and Québec c'est beau. The selected definition links avoir beau at L396; following examples show avoir beau plus an infinitive. The field is confined to unsuccessful effort, not every possible concessive use of avoir beau.

usage.proposed_usage: Masculine singular abstract noun referring to what is excellent or admirable.
usage.scope_restrictions: The noun for a handsome man, fair weather, adjective and adverb are excluded.
usage.accepted_usage: Masculine singular abstract noun referring to what is excellent or admirable.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: The singular abstract noun selects what is excellent/perfect/admirable in its kind. EN and ZH preserve that broad excellence sense, rather than substituting a handsome man or exclusively aesthetic beauty. The source's singular/invariable noun heading applies.

usage.proposed_usage: Masculine noun used as a polite form of direct address to a man.
usage.scope_restrictions: Historical household ranks, irony and dialect senses are excluded; this sense does not cover Mr before a surname.
usage.accepted_usage: Masculine noun used as a polite form of direct address to a man.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: Sir/先生 is polite direct address to a man, supported by Bonjour, monsieur at L11. The usage expressly excludes Mr before a surname, irony and historical ranks. IPA mə.sjø is the current headword value, not the obsolete pronunciations in the later pronunciation note.

usage.proposed_usage: Adjective for physical size or height compared with similar beings or things.
usage.scope_restrictions: Fame, honorific titles, quantities, capital letters and noun or adverb uses are excluded.
usage.accepted_usage: Adjective for physical size or height compared with similar beings or things.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: Large/big/tall and 大的、高大的 describe comparable physical dimensions. EN explicitly covers a person's height; ZH agrees. Removing long duration and specialist uses is an honest narrowing of the source. The current long comparison text is contributor wording, not the separate historical noun body.

usage.proposed_usage: Masculine noun in children's speech for an adult.
usage.scope_restrictions: Elite persons, nobility, large objects and vocative encouragement of children are excluded.
usage.accepted_usage: Masculine noun in children's speech for an adult.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: The noun means a grown-up/adult in children's speech. The broader current source says older person, even adult; selecting the adult part is valid. The vocative use addressing a child and social-elite senses are excluded. Masculine grand is retained without denying possible feminine forms elsewhere.

usage.proposed_usage: Noun of either grammatical gender for a child before adolescence.
usage.scope_restrictions: An offspring of any age, descendants and figurative or adjectival uses are excluded.
usage.accepted_usage: Noun of either grammatical gender for a child before adolescence.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: Child/儿童 selects a person before adolescence, exactly the current contributor definition. It does not mean offspring of any age or all legal minors. The noun's either-gender marking is retained in usage.

usage.proposed_usage: Transitive verb for hearing a sound.
usage.scope_restrictions: Understanding, intentions, judicial hearings and the pronominal relationship sense are excluded.
usage.accepted_usage: Transitive verb for hearing a sound.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: Hear/perceive a sound/听见 agrees with the selected transitive sensory use. Understanding, intention, court hearings and the pronominal relationship are excluded. The source verb heading and infinitive IPA are appropriate.

usage.proposed_usage: Temporal preposition followed by an elapsed duration, with the frozen subclass PRE retained.
usage.scope_restrictions: The presentative verb meaning here is or there is is excluded; /vwa.la/ is the selected IPA variant.
usage.accepted_usage: Temporal preposition followed by an elapsed duration, with the frozen subclass PRE retained.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: Ago/……以前 is the temporal preposition with elapsed duration. Source PRE heading L110 and definition L112 are separate from the presentative. The following quoted examples provide construction facts only: voilà quinze jours; the literary sentences are not proposed for redistribution. The field wording is an original explanatory adaptation, not copied quotation prose.

usage.proposed_usage: Transitive verb for searching for a person or thing.
usage.scope_restrictions: Fetching, provoking a fight, chercher à with an infinitive and pronominal introspection are excluded.
usage.accepted_usage: Transitive verb for searching for a person or thing.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: Look for/search for/寻找 describes efforts to find a person or thing. It is transitive; the fetching, provocative and chercher à + infinitive senses are excluded. Current trouver rather than historic découvrir does not change this selected use.

usage.proposed_usage: Feminine noun for the time unit hour.
usage.scope_restrictions: Clock time, appointments, death, angular measures and religious books are excluded.
usage.accepted_usage: Feminine noun for the time unit hour.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: Hour equals 60 minutes/3,600 seconds in all meanings. The technical label on the source does not make this everyday time unit a specialist exception. Clock time, appointment, angular and religious senses are excluded. The original modern unit explanation predates the DAF merge.

usage.proposed_usage: Adverb comparing how an action is performed.
usage.scope_restrictions: Adjective and noun uses, health as a state and the dialect meaning more are excluded.
usage.accepted_usage: Adverb comparing how an action is performed.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: Better/更好地 is the comparative of adverb bien and describes a manner. The nominal, adjective, health-state and regional more senses are separate. DAF7 MIEUX independently contains the exact accomplished/advantageous wording, so its surviving expression can be traced earlier than DAF8.

usage.proposed_usage: Masculine noun for an improvement in health or condition.
usage.scope_restrictions: The abstract best, comparative adverb and adjective are excluded.
usage.accepted_usage: Masculine noun for an improvement in health or condition.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: Improvement in condition, particularly health, matches meilleur état/meilleure santé. EN/ZH preserve the masculine noun and il y a du mieux construction. The superlative/best-of-one's-ability noun is not substituted. Current source NOM heading L55 and definition L60 are explicit.

usage.proposed_usage: Temporal adverb for a state or result already reached.
usage.scope_restrictions: The forgotten-information use and the frozen ONO group are excluded.
usage.accepted_usage: Temporal adverb for a state or result already reached.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: Already/已经 describes a change or result attained by the reference time, preserving the present/past reference in the source. Forgotten-information déjà and reactive ONO are excluded. The modern criterion/change-of-state wording is distinct from the DAF-era dès à présent definition.

usage.proposed_usage: Plural possessive determiner for one person addressed with tu; frozen ADJ:pos is retained.
usage.scope_restrictions: Plural addressees, polite vous and singular possessed nouns are excluded; /tɛ/ is the selected recorded variant.
usage.accepted_usage: Plural possessive determiner for one person addressed with tu; frozen ADJ:pos is retained.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: Tes is plural your addressed to one person using tu. Both noun genders are covered; plural addressees and polite vous are excluded. Source L19 links plural ton/ta and L20-L21 give plural possessed nouns. L24 explicitly documents the older adjectif possessif name, supporting frozen ADJ:pos.

usage.proposed_usage: Verb for helping a person carry out an action, including aider quelqu'un à followed by an infinitive.
usage.scope_restrictions: Impersonal facilitation and pronominal se servir de are excluded; /e.de/ is the selected recorded variant.
usage.accepted_usage: Verb for helping a person carry out an action, including aider quelqu'un à followed by an infinitive.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: Help someone carry out an action/帮助某人 agrees with the source contributor facilitation definition. Source L17 actually demonstrates aider mon frère à porter. Impersonal facilitation and pronominal se servir de are excluded. The fact that the following source senses differ does not broaden this one.

usage.proposed_usage: Feminine noun for a mother through giving birth.
usage.scope_restrictions: The separately recorded caregiving relationship, animal mothers, religious titles and figurative origins are excluded.
usage.accepted_usage: Feminine noun for a mother through giving birth.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: Birth mother only: the woman has given birth to at least one child. EN/ZH retain that restriction. The caregiving/adoptive, animal and religious senses are excluded. The earlier contributor state separates birth and caregiving; the current source has modern, independently phrased birth wording.

usage.proposed_usage: Verb for an attempt, in essayer de followed by an infinitive.
usage.scope_restrictions: Testing equipment, trying on clothes, mineral analysis and pronominal uses are excluded; /e.se.je/ is the selected variant.
usage.accepted_usage: Verb for an attempt, in essayer de followed by an infinitive.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: Try/attempt/尝试 selects essayer de + infinitive, not testing equipment or trying on clothing. The source tenter/oser supplies the attempt sense; following examples explicitly contain essayer de. This is not an assertion that oser is always interchangeable with essayer. The selected IPA is the recorded e.se.je variant.

usage.proposed_usage: Interrogative adjective before a noun, with frozen ADJ:int retained.
usage.scope_restrictions: The pronoun before être, quality questions and exclamations are excluded.
usage.accepted_usage: Interrogative adjective before a noun, with frozen ADJ:int retained.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: Which/what/哪一个、什么 selects interrogative quel before a noun and asks identity. Current adjective-interrogative heading, form template and quelle/quelles examples support agreement with that noun. Predicate pronoun, quality-question and exclamative uses are excluded; frozen ADJ:int is retained.

usage.proposed_usage: Plural possessive determiner with plural or polite-singular vous; frozen ADJ:pos retained.
usage.scope_restrictions: Singular possessed nouns and the abbreviation for versos are excluded.
usage.accepted_usage: Plural possessive determiner with plural or polite-singular vous; frozen ADJ:pos retained.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: Vos is plural possessed nouns with either multiple addressees or one polite-singular vous addressee. EN/ZH preserve both choices and exclude singular possessed nouns. Current L10 states the two cases explicitly; L16 documents the historical possessive-adjective terminology.

usage.proposed_usage: Temporal adverb used absolutely with an understood starting point.
usage.scope_restrictions: The preposition with an expressed complement, spatial uses and depuis que are excluded.
usage.accepted_usage: Temporal adverb used absolutely with an understood starting point.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: Since then/从那以后 is an absolute temporal adverb with an understood starting time. Source L132 explicitly has Depuis, je n'en ai plus entendu parler; L139 translates since then. It is separate from the preposition and depuis que.

usage.proposed_usage: Temporal preposition followed by a starting point or duration continuing to a reference time.
usage.scope_restrictions: Spatial or rank uses, the adverb and obsolete infinitive constructions are excluded.
usage.accepted_usage: Temporal preposition followed by a starting point or duration continuing to a reference time.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: Since/for/自从、已有……时间 selects a temporal starting point or duration extending to a reference time. The temporal preposition heading and depuis longtemps/depuis peu de temps examples support this. Spatial and rank uses beginning at L17 are excluded. The reference may be past, not only the present.

usage.proposed_usage: Masculine singular indefinite pronoun; frozen ASCII apostrophe remains bound to source quelqu’un.
usage.scope_restrictions: Important-person, obsolete one-of-several and plural uses are excluded.
usage.accepted_usage: Masculine singular indefinite pronoun; frozen ASCII apostrophe remains bound to source quelqu’un.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: Someone/某人 selects an existing person with identity unimportant or unspecified. The pronoun is masculine singular, not an important-person noun or plural. The ASCII frozen headword is explicitly linked to the curly-apostrophe source by the actual retained revision 35035 redirect. This is a provenance binding; it does not require adding a search alias or changing saved identities.

usage.proposed_usage: Quantity adverb modifying an action, as in travailler beaucoup.
usage.scope_restrictions: The determiner beaucoup de, pronoun, comparison intensifier and considérablement sense are excluded.
usage.accepted_usage: Quantity adverb modifying an action, as in travailler beaucoup.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: A lot/much/很多、大量地 is quantity applied to an action. The field does not admit the determiner beaucoup de, comparative intensification or the separately listed considérablement sense. The short quantity wording expresses a lexical fact; current translations/adaptations retain CC BY-SA attribution.

usage.proposed_usage: Intransitive verb for returning to a place.
usage.scope_restrictions: Reappearance, costs, changed opinions, recovery and cooking are excluded; /ʁə.vniʁ/ is the selected recorded variant.
usage.accepted_usage: Intransitive verb for returning to a place.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: Come back/return/回来 selects return to the place one left. Reappearance, costs, opinion changes, recovery and cooking are excluded. The infinitive and its recorded schwa-elision variant are retained.

usage.proposed_usage: Consequence connector with frozen CON retained; the source calls it an adverbe conjonctif.
usage.scope_restrictions: Surprise, pressing requests, emphasis and return-from-digression uses are excluded; /dɔ̃k/ is the selected variant.
usage.accepted_usage: Consequence connector with frozen CON retained; the source calls it an adverbe conjonctif.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: Therefore/so/因此、所以 expresses result or consequence. Current adverbe conjonctif explicitly supports the connector function of frozen CON; no source claim that this is a lexical coordinating conjunction is added. Surprise, requests and discourse-resumption readings are excluded. The selected dɔ̃k variant is recorded with dɔ̃ as an alternative.

usage.accepted_usage: Masculine noun for an expression of thanks, un merci.
usage.scope_restrictions: The old feminine mercy noun and the interjection.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: Masculine un merci means an expression of thanks; the old feminine mercy noun is excluded.

usage.accepted_usage: Polite interjection expressing thanks; frozen ONO corresponds to the source interjection.
usage.scope_restrictions: Requests, polite refusal, Quebec intensifier and noun uses.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: The gratitude interjection maps to frozen ONO. Requests, refusal, Quebec intensification and the noun are excluded.

usage.accepted_usage: Third-person possessive determiner sa before a consonant-initial feminine singular noun.
usage.scope_restrictions: Plural forms, vowel-initial contexts requiring son, and the language-name noun.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: Sa selects a feminine singular possessed noun before a consonant; third-person possessor gender does not determine the form.

usage.accepted_usage: Indefinite adjective describing a different identity of the same type.
usage.scope_restrictions: Superior merit, figurative resemblance and standalone pronoun uses.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: Indefinite adjective for a different identity of the same type; no standalone-pronoun or superior-merit substitution.

usage.accepted_usage: Article/determiner-bearing indefinite pronoun, l’autre or un autre; the source places this use under nom, while modern corroboration calls it a pronoun.
usage.scope_restrictions: Adjectival use before a noun and philosophical otherness.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: Determiner-bearing l’autre/un autre has pronoun function. Fixed French nominal subsection and retained Robert pronom support the exact PRO:ind mapping.

accuracy_corroboration.finding: Modern entry labels the standalone determiner-bearing use as pronom; Wiktionnaire labels the same use nom.

usage.accepted_usage: Possessive determiner ta for a singular addressee and consonant-initial feminine singular noun.
usage.scope_restrictions: Plural forms, vowel-initial contexts requiring ton, noun and regional verb uses.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: Ta addresses one person as tu and determines a feminine singular noun before a consonant; ton/vowel and plural uses excluded.

usage.accepted_usage: Intransitive arrival at a destination.
usage.scope_restrictions: Success, events happening, social advancement and nautical uses.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: Intransitive arrival at a destination, including the documented default speaker location without a complement; not success or events happening.

usage.accepted_usage: Plural demonstrative determiner ces; selected /se/ before a consonant.
usage.scope_restrictions: Singular forms, noun use, alternative /sɛ/ and vowel liaison.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: Ces is the plural demonstrative of either gender. /se/ is a recorded variant; consonant context excludes vowel liaison and the alternative /sɛ/.

usage.accepted_usage: Transitive giving of owned property without payment.
usage.scope_restrictions: Payment, exchange, punishment and pronominal uses.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: Direct transitive gift of owned property without payment. All three meanings retain the gratuitous transfer, excluding payment and exchange.

usage.accepted_usage: Direct transitive visual attention, regarder quelqu’un ou quelque chose.
usage.scope_restrictions: Concern, assessment, physical orientation and pronominal uses.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: Direct visual attention to a person or thing; the source permits several valencies but the selected direct-transitive use is explicit.

usage.accepted_usage: Temporal adverb of continuation.
usage.scope_restrictions: Again, addition, degree comparison, restriction and pas encore.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: Temporal continuation is still, not repetition again or the negative construction pas encore.

usage.accepted_usage: Direct transitive telephone contact.
usage.scope_restrictions: Naming, summoning by voice, animal cries and reciprocal s’appeler.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: Telephone contact is explicitly source-labelled transitive or reciprocal; selecting appeler quelqu’un preserves the direct-transitive subset.

usage.accepted_usage: Direct interrogative marker; frozen ADV retained, source taxonomy particule; unelided headword IPA.
usage.scope_restrictions: Popular indirect-question use and analysis as an ordinary lexical adverb; elided-form IPA.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: The fixed particle is the same direct-question opener in frozen ADV. The mapping preserves the exact target without asserting an ordinary lexical adverb; subject order and vowel elision are correct.

source_binding_evidence.reason: Question-opening marker, not a claim that Wiktionnaire labels it adverbe.

usage.accepted_usage: Quantity/frequency adverb meaning not much.
usage.scope_restrictions: Degree before adjectives, determiner-like peu de, standalone pronoun and noun uses.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: Quantity/frequency peu is little/not much; source examples support quantitative scope. Degree before adjectives, peu de and nominal/pronominal uses are excluded.

usage.accepted_usage: Masculine singular-only noun for a small quantity.
usage.scope_restrictions: Adverb, indefinite pronoun and plural noun forms.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: Small quantity in the masculine singular-only noun section. All meanings retain that restriction and exclude the adverb.

usage.accepted_usage: Adult male human, as distinct from a woman or child.
usage.scope_restrictions: Generic humanity, husband, subordinate and scientific genus uses.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: Adult male human selected, with the source gender/sex distinction; generic humanity, husband and specialist genus uses are excluded.

usage.accepted_usage: Intransitive departure from a place.
usage.scope_restrictions: Origin, starting machinery, dying, archaic division and regional transitive uses.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: Literal intransitive departure from one place for another; no transitive, archaic division or figurative origin sense.

usage.accepted_usage: First-person singular possessor with plural possessed noun; selected /mɛ/ before a consonant.
usage.scope_restrictions: Singular possessed nouns, alternative /me/ and vowel liaison.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: Mes concerns one first-person possessor and plural possessed entities. /mɛ/ is explicitly recorded; consonant scope excludes liaison.

usage.accepted_usage: Temporal adverb of continuous duration.
usage.scope_restrictions: Usually, still, nevertheless and concessive uses.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: Continuous duration without interruption; excludes the usually/still/concessive readings.

usage.accepted_usage: Calendar day of twenty-four hours.
usage.scope_restrictions: Daylight, agricultural measure, date-specific and figurative senses.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: Calendar day as a generally midnight-starting 24-hour period, rather than daylight. Source modern nominal use supports all explanations.

usage.accepted_usage: Adult female human, as distinct from a girl.
usage.scope_restrictions: Spouse, stereotyped qualities, domestic staff and appositional uses.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: Adult female human, not spouse or girl. Feminine noun and source gender/sex distinction remain aligned.

usage.accepted_usage: Temporal duration or interval between events.
usage.scope_restrictions: Weather, mythological personification, grammatical tense and musical beat.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: Temporal duration or interval between events; masculine invariant spelling temps is evidenced, not weather, tense or musical beat.

usage.accepted_usage: Adverb referring to the present time; selected /mɛ̃t.nɑ̃/ variant.
usage.scope_restrictions: Henceforth, contrastive discourse use and maintenir participle.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: Present moment/current period; /mɛ̃t.nɑ̃/ is an explicitly recorded pronunciation variant, not a fabricated normalized form.

usage.accepted_usage: First-person plural possessors and singular possessed noun.
usage.scope_restrictions: Royal/editorial plural for one possessor, plural nos, language noun and accented nôtre pronoun.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: Our: multiple possessors including the speaker and a singular possessed noun. Notre remains distinct from the accented pronoun nôtre and plural nos.

usage.accepted_usage: Human lifetime from birth to death.
usage.scope_restrictions: Biological processes, lifestyle, livelihood, biography and regional road noun.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: Human lifetime from birth to death is a valid narrowing of the selected duration sense; not biological processes or lifestyle.

usage.accepted_usage: Cardinal numeral before a consonant-initial noun; frozen ADJ:num.
usage.scope_restrictions: Postposed ordinal use, noun uses and liaison before a vowel.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: Preposed cardinal two is the exact ADJ:num use. /dø/ applies in the selected consonant context, excluding vowel liaison, ordinal and noun uses.

usage.accepted_usage: Direct transitive placement in a specified location.
usage.scope_restrictions: Clothing, figurative situations, sexual ellipse and pronominal uses.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: Direct placement of a person, animal or thing in a location; excludes clothing, figurative situations and pronominal uses.

usage.accepted_usage: Intransitive remaining at a physical location; selected /ʁɛs.te/ variant.
usage.scope_restrictions: Continuing states, remaining quantities, obligations and regional dwelling sense.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: Source combines place and state; selecting remaining in a physical place is accurate. /ʁɛs.te/ is explicitly recorded.

usage.accepted_usage: Preposition before a nominal complement expressing absence.
usage.scope_restrictions: Infinitival sans + infinitive construction.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: Nominal-complement without: absence/exclusion and normally omitted indefinite/partitive article are retained; infinitival construction excluded.

usage.accepted_usage: Adjective denoting absence of company.
usage.scope_restrictions: Only/unique before a noun, musical solo, adverbial use and nominal use.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: Alone without company in the adjective section, not unique/only before a noun, musical solo or the nominal use.

usage.accepted_usage: Nominal masculine un seul referring to one person; source elliptical adjective use supported by uncited examples and modern noun corroboration.
usage.scope_restrictions: Adjective meaning alone, musical solo and interpretation as a lonely-person noun.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: Un seul denotes one person. Fixed lines 47–49 demonstrate substantive ellipsis; retained Robert explicitly labels the corresponding construction nom. This supports NOM without a lonely-person substitution.

accuracy_corroboration.finding: Modern entry explicitly labels un/une seul(e) as nom; only the one-person subset is proposed.

usage.accepted_usage: Direct transitive stopping of movement; selected /a.ʁe.te/ variant.
usage.scope_restrictions: Arrest, decisions, stopping an activity and pronominal s’arrêter.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: Direct-transitive stopping of movement is the selected literal sense. /a.ʁe.te/ is a recorded variant; arrest and stopping an activity excluded.

usage.accepted_usage: Adverb confirming reality.
usage.scope_restrictions: Degree intensifier and interjection of surprise.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: Reality-confirming really/actually, not the degree intensifier or surprise interjection.

usage.accepted_usage: Direct transitive familiarity acquired through experience; original connaître spelling.
usage.scope_restrictions: Knowing a fact expressed by savoir, legal jurisdiction, sexual and pronominal uses.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: Experience-based familiarity with a person/thing; exact traditional connaître spelling is explicitly source-labelled. Knowing a fact with savoir and legal/pronominal senses excluded.

usage.accepted_usage: Singular indefinite determiner with an uncountable noun; selected /kɛlk/ variant.
usage.scope_restrictions: Literary singular countable use, plural quelques, concessive and approximate adverb uses.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: Singular quelque with an uncountable noun indicates a small unspecified amount. The separate literary countable and plural/concessive uses are excluded; /kɛlk/ is recorded.

usage.accepted_usage: Approximation adverb before a numeral; selected /kɛlk/ variant.
usage.scope_restrictions: Concessive quelque + adjective/adverb + que and determiner uses.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: Invariable approximation before a numeral, not the determiner or concessive construction. /kɛlk/ is a source-recorded variant.

usage.accepted_usage: Adjective expressing a person’s certainty, être sûr de quelque chose.
usage.scope_restrictions: Safe places, reliable people, inevitable events and regional adverb.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: A person’s absence of doubt in être sûr de quelque chose, not safety or reliability of objects; all explanations retain the chosen construction.

usage.accepted_usage: Adjective denoting fairness or justice.
usage.scope_restrictions: Exact fit, insufficient size, musical intervals and noun/adverb uses.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: Fair/just is correctly selected. French and English match the source. Chinese 权利 confuses entitlement with the legal/equitable meaning of droit in this definition; replace it with 法理.

usage.accepted_usage: Restrictive adverb meaning only.
usage.scope_restrictions: Exactness, musical pitch, insufficient fit, informal intensifier and attenuative pragmatics.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: Restrictive just/only matches the simple/only source sense; pitch, exactness, informal intensification and attenuative pragmatics excluded.

usage.accepted_usage: Human noun denoting a person acting or judging equitably.
usage.scope_restrictions: Abstract justice, religious righteousness and adjective/adverb uses.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: The untagged extended human noun for acting/judging equitably is a separate source sense before the religion-tagged sense. The proposed secular restriction is supported.

usage.accepted_usage: Literal transitive causation of death; selected broad definition line 30.
usage.scope_restrictions: Figurative destruction, hyperbolic fatigue, time-killing and pronominal suicide.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: Literal causing death is narrowed to people/animals in direct-transitive tuer; no figurative destruction, fatigue or suicide sense.

usage.accepted_usage: Feminine noun la mort: death as the cessation of vital functions.

usage.proposed_usage: Causal subordinating conjunction introducing a reason clause.
usage.accepted_usage: Causal subordinating conjunction introducing a reason clause.

usage.proposed_usage: Transitive non-reflexive verb: lose something previously possessed.
usage.accepted_usage: Transitive non-reflexive verb: lose something previously possessed.

usage.proposed_usage: Feminine affectionate noun for one’s mother; not limited to small children.
usage.accepted_usage: Feminine affectionate noun for one’s mother; not limited to small children.

usage.everyday_sense_reason: Maman is an affectionate noun for one’s mother at any age. Mum/mom and 妈妈 preserve that register and relation; adult children are explicitly included.

usage.proposed_usage: Transitive non-reflexive verb: perceive an odour.
usage.accepted_usage: Transitive non-reflexive verb: perceive an odour.
usage.scope_restrictions: Emitting a smell, touch, emotional feeling and reflexive se sentir are excluded.
usage.everyday_sense_reason: Perceiving an odour is transitive sentir, not emitting a smell or se sentir. English smell is disambiguated by the explanation and Chinese 闻到 is correct.

usage.proposed_usage: Informal affirmative response retained as frozen ouais/ADV; the source labels the same use an interjection.

Surprise, joy and mere acknowledgement are excluded; no owner exception or blanket interjection-to-adverb mapping is inferred.
usage.source_binding_gap: Both fixed Wiktionnaire and captured Le Robert classify affirmative ouais as an interjection. No exact modern ADV source has been established; the Lexique taxonomy correspondence remains unresolved.

usage.proposed_usage: Intransitive non-reflexive verb: be alive.

usage.proposed_usage: Adjective for ordinal position one; retain frozen ADJ rather than changing it to ADJ:num.
usage.accepted_usage: Adjective for ordinal position one; retain frozen ADJ rather than changing it to ADJ:num.

usage.proposed_usage: Masculine noun for the person who precedes all others, with attested feminine première.
usage.accepted_usage: Masculine noun for the person who precedes all others, with attested feminine première.

usage.proposed_usage: Masculine noun for an everyday difficulty, with the source’s familiar register retained.

usage.accepted_usage: Transitive non-reflexive verb: hold something firmly in the hands.

usage.proposed_usage: Feminine noun: the human hand.
usage.accepted_usage: Feminine noun: the human hand.

usage.proposed_usage: Adverb: quickly or at speed.
usage.accepted_usage: Adverb: quickly or at speed.

usage.everyday_sense_reason: Vite is the adverb quickly/fast, not an adjective or imperative interjection. /vit/ and all three definitions match.

usage.accepted_usage: Comparative adverb for a lower quantity or degree; select the recorded /mwɛ̃/ variant.

usage.accepted_usage: Masculine noun for the ordinary written minus sign, identical in singular and plural.

usage.accepted_usage: Transitive non-reflexive verb: lose the memory of someone or something.

usage.accepted_usage: Masculine noun: atmospheric air.

usage.accepted_usage: Masculine noun: the act or mark of greeting someone, not the standalone interjection.

usage.proposed_usage: Temporal adverb: the day immediately following the day of speaking.
